decisions.question: Which Outline activities are most exposed to AI delegation today, and how exposed?
decisions.answer:
Seven of the 14 mapped activities have observed Anthropic data. The three highest-autonomy matches sit on visual-language definition, identity-system build, and audience-research synthesis — all activities owned by senior people. The pattern is the inverse of what the studio's pricing assumes: the work that is most signature today (the visual-language work the design lead does on every engagement) is the work where the closest matched task in the Anthropic sample shows Claude operating with high autonomy.

This is a pattern, not a verdict — the Anthropic sample observes a different population running different briefs. What it does say: do not assume the senior-craft layer is naturally insulated.

decisions.question: Where is the line between AI assisting and AI working alone in this studio?
decisions.answer:
The middle band of the map — where Claude was observed assisting tasks under supervision — covers most of strategy: brand positioning, audience research, competitive audit. The studio's strategy lead can plausibly take on more engagements with the same hours by leaning into this band.

The upper band — where Claude was observed working most autonomously on the closest matched tasks — covers the visual-language and identity-system-build work, which is design's signature output. Here the studio's bet should be the opposite: keep the work in human hands, and price it as the work that can only be done by named people (Lena, design lead).

decisions.question: What should change about hours allocation given this map?
decisions.answer:
Today senior designers spend most of their time on UI design and identity-system production — both of which sit in the upper band of the closest Anthropic sample, where Claude works with high autonomy on similar tasks. That hours mix made sense when the production layer was the bottleneck. It will not age well.

Move: the operations lead reviews how senior hours were spent in Q1 2026 and re-targets at least 20% of them upstream — onto positioning briefs, brand-book authorship, and visual-language definition. The brand book is the artefact the studio is best known for; the senior people who currently produce its supporting material should be co-authoring it.

decisions.question: Which capability is missing from the org and would compound across these activities?
decisions.answer:
The map shows that audience research and competitive audit (both strategy activities) sit in the middle band — where Claude is observed materially assisting similar tasks in the Anthropic sample. Today the studio runs these one engagement at a time; the insights from each engagement leave with the deliverable.

The missing capability: a context-keeping practice that captures the prior-engagement work into a queryable shape, so the next engagement starts from cumulative context rather than zero. This is the role the next hire owns. Every engagement that walks past this hire compounds the next one's pitch.
